The Vault v0.6.5 fixes saved summaries being cut off after save, makes recall summaries stick to what is actually in memory, and makes Graphify work on large projects without leaking secret files into the graph.

## Saved summaries are no longer cut off

- **Root cause.** After every save, an AI "polish" step rewrote the summary with a 500-token limit and saved whatever came back, even when the model stopped mid-sentence. The original text was not kept anywhere.
- **Fix.** Post-save enrichment no longer touches summaries. The text the agent or user wrote is the source of truth. AI tag suggestions still run.
- Existing installs: summaries already cut off are not repaired automatically. If you need to recover them, the original text is usually still in the saving agent's session transcript.

## More accurate recall

- **Grounded `context_summary`.** The summary is built only from memories that match the query, and the model is told to use only what those memories say. When nothing matches, there is no summary instead of generic advice.
- **Matches from other projects.** A project-scoped recall with a query now also returns `cross_project_matches`: up to 3 memories from other projects that contain the query phrase or an exact keyword. The project's own results are unchanged.
- **`vault_find_memory` keywords** now find an item when any term appears in its keywords, title, subject, summary or content. Before, every keyword had to equal an element of the keyword list exactly.

## Graphify on large projects

- The default graph read limit is now 64 MB (was 8 MB), so 20–40 MB graphs work without passing `max_bytes`. When a graph is still too large, the error states the `max_bytes` value to retry with.
- A parsed graph is cached while `graph.json` is unchanged, so repeated queries no longer re-read and re-parse it.
- `GRAPH_REPORT.md` is read in full and `max_report_bytes` limits only the snippets returned. This removes the "exceeds the read budget" caveat that appeared on successful `explain_impact` calls.

## Graphify source scope and secrets

- Builds now skip more credential files: `*recovery-codes*`, `credentials.json`, `secrets.*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.p12`, `*.pfx`, `*.jks`, `*.keystore`, `*.kdbx`, `*.ppk`, SSH keys (`id_rsa`, `id_ed25519`, …), `.npmrc`, `.pypirc`, `.netrc`, `.git-credentials`, `.htpasswd`, and `.ssh/`, `.aws/`, `.gnupg/` folders. Rebuild existing graphs to drop files that were indexed before.
- Add a `.graphifyignore` file to a project's source root to exclude more paths (gitignore-style: `*`, `**`, `?`, a leading `/` anchors to the root; `!` negation is not supported).
- Graphify status warns when the source root is a plain folder holding several separate projects, such as a git clone next to an extracted archive of the same repo, which would duplicate every node.
- Builds record the branch and commit that were checked out in the source manifest and build log, since the graph reflects that checkout rather than the remote branch.
- The status message no longer claims manual builds arrive "in a later phase".

## Verification

- Full automated suite: 56 test files, 405 tests.
- Core, CLI, MCP server, and desktop type checks pass.

This build packages the desktop app and the bundled `vault-memory` MCP sidecar runtime. After installing, open The Vault and use Settings -> Client setup to connect Codex, Claude Desktop, or Claude Code.
